raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 has 12 local MLA heads at TP8. `_concat_and_cast_mha_k` currently requires a power-of-two head count before calling the Triton helper, even though that helper already handles padded head counts. These shapes fall back to two separate tensor copies.

## Modifications

Remove the redundant head-count restriction at the shared model dispatch point. Reuse the existing masked concat kernel and keep the feature-dimension guards and the 128-head specialized path.

For FA3 with FP8 KV storage, these head counts now follow the same output-dtype rule as the existing power-of-two Triton path. Other covered backends retain the input dtype.

## Accuracy Tests

Upstream `b146a8576de930cf3adc104e601feb2790cdf3f6` plus this PR only, NVIDIA B30Z (B300), PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and Triton 3.8.0:

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_concat_mla.py -k model_mha_k_concat -q
# 14 passed, 94 deselected
```

The tests call the actual model helper and Triton implementation. Coverage includes BF16 / FP16, empty and 64K-token inputs, 12 / 24 heads, an 8-head control, strided inputs, and repeated CUDA Graph replay with changed inputs. Outputs match the reference exactly. The FA3 dtype case compares raw FP8 bytes for finite random inputs against the reference cast.

Full-model accuracy and serving throughput have not been rerun on this branch; the results below are isolated operator timings.

### Upstream CUDA validation

The complete registered `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_concat_mla.py` passed on the upstream H100 CI runner for head `81955274f6363c91979dd12d05e2662621bc4346`: **108 passed, 0 skipped**, including all 14 new model-helper cases and the existing JIT/AOT regressions. [Passing CI job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41299322000/job/124900828609).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Isolated concat operator on one NVIDIA B30Z, 12 heads, `nope_dim=128`, `rope_dim=64`, BF16 output and strided KV / latent views. Baseline is the exact two-copy fallback at the base commit; patched runs the model helper. Both allocate their output. Eager execution, no profiler and no CUDA Graph; `triton.testing.do_bench`, 25 ms warmup and 100 ms measurement, median CUDA-event latency, L2 flush per sample. Baseline / patched order alternates across five rounds.

| Tokens | Baseline, 5 rounds (μs) | Patched, 5 rounds (μs) | Median latency reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 11.328, 11.264, 11.328, 11.264, 11.264 | 6.272, 6.304, 6.240, 6.240, 6.304 | 44.32% |
| 8,192 | 50.112, 50.112, 50.112, 50.112, 50.144 | 16.448, 16.576, 16.576, 16.480, 16.480 | 67.11% |
| 65,536 | 310.240, 310.240, 310.240, 310.240, 310.240 | 82.080, 82.112, 82.272, 82.560, 82.080 | 73.53% |

These are operator timings, not an end-to-end throughput result. No full-model speedup is inferred from the percentages.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed files with the repository's isort / Ruff rules; AST, whitespace and registered-test checks pass.
- [x] Add regression coverage to registered test suites.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- [x] Complete registered concat CUDA regression suite in upstream CI (108 passed, 0 skipped). Full-model measurements are outside this isolated-operator claim.

@@ -1,5 +1,7 @@
 import itertools
 import sys
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
 
 import pytest
 import torch
@@ -90,6 +92,100 @@ def jit_concat_mla_absorb_q(
 NUM_TOKENS_LIST = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024]
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "num_tokens,num_heads",
+    [(0, 12), (1, 12), (17, 12), (257, 24), (19, 8), (65536, 12)],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+def test_model_mha_k_concat(num_tokens, num_heads, dtype):
+    """Exercise model dispatch with strided KV projection and latent RoPE views."""
+    from sglang.srt.models.deepseek_common.attention_forward_methods import forward_mha
+
+    attn = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_local_heads=num_heads,
+        qk_nope_head_dim=128,
+        qk_rope_head_dim=64,
+        qk_head_dim=192,
+        current_attention_backend="trtllm_mla",
+        kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3",
+    )
+    kv = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_heads, 256, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    latent = torch.randn(num_tokens, 1, 576, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    k_nope, k_rope = kv[..., :128], latent[..., 512:]
+    expected = torch.empty(num_tokens, num_heads, 192, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    torch_concat_mla_k(expected, k_nope, k_rope)
+    with patch.object(
+        forward_mha,
+        "concat_and_cast_mha_k_triton",
+        wraps=forward_mha.concat_and_cast_mha_k_triton,
+    ) as concat:
+        actual = forward_mha.DeepseekMHAForwardMixin._concat_and_cast_mha_k(
+            attn, k_nope, k_rope, None
+        )
+    concat.assert_called_once()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_model_mha_k_concat_graph():
+    from sglang.srt.models.deepseek_common.attention_forward_methods import forward_mha
+
+    attn = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_local_heads=12,
+        qk_nope_head_dim=128,
+        qk_rope_head_dim=64,
+        qk_head_dim=192,
+        current_attention_backend="trtllm_mla",
+        kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3",
+    )
+    kv = torch.randn(17, 12, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    latent = torch.randn(17, 1, 576, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_nope, k_rope = kv[..., :128], latent[..., 512:]
+    concat = forward_mha.DeepseekMHAForwardMixin._concat_and_cast_mha_k
+    concat(attn, k_nope, k_rope, None)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        actual = concat(attn, k_nope, k_rope, None)
+    for _ in range(2):
+        kv.normal_()
+        latent.normal_()
+        graph.replay()
+        expected = torch.empty_like(actual)
+        torch_concat_mla_k(expected, k_nope, k_rope)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_model_mha_k_concat_fa3_fp8():
+    from sglang.srt.models.deepseek_common.attention_forward_methods import forward_mha
+
+    attn = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_local_heads=12,
+        qk_nope_head_dim=128,
+        qk_rope_head_dim=64,
+        qk_head_dim=192,
+        current_attention_backend="fa3",
+        kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3",
+    )
+    k_nope = torch.randn(17, 12, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k_rope = torch.randn(17, 1, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    expected = torch.empty(17, 12, 192, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    torch_concat_mla_k(expected, k_nope, k_rope)
+    with patch.object(
+        forward_mha,
+        "get_token_to_kv_pool",
+        return_value=SimpleNamespace(dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+    ):
+        actual = forward_mha.DeepseekMHAForwardMixin._concat_and_cast_mha_k(
+            attn, k_nope, k_rope, None
+        )
+    assert actual.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        actual.view(torch.uint8),
+        expected.to(actual.dtype).view(torch.uint8),
+        rtol=0,
+        atol=0,
+    )
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", NUM_TOKENS_LIST)
 def test_concat_mla_k_jit_vs_torch(num_tokens: int) -> None:
     """Test JIT kernel against PyTorch reference."""
